correctness.rationale: Exact graph definition and closed-neighborhood GF2 equations. Eliminating inner variables gives period-five first differences, hence period-ten outer sequence. Cyclic boundary forces four parameter cases; the thirty-two five-bit motifs have rigorously exhausted weights 3,5,7 with multiplicities 10,12,10, and the additional thirty-two twisted ten-bit configurations all have half the vertices. Direct GF2 Gauss-Jordan for all 5<=n<=60 and independent ten-periodic-pattern enumeration for all 5<=n<=100, each with original-equation checks, reproduce all cardinality histograms. Finite computation is supplementary to the algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: The same-family homogeneous closed-neighborhood kernel and its weight spectrum were obtained in earlier related work, and Torrence–Torrence (2016) gave nullity information. The present exact polynomial is for the inhomogeneous all-ones syndrome coset (odd dominating sets), which is not determined by the ordinary kernel weight enumerator alone. Primary Caro 2001 and 2003 sources, Hatzl–Wagner 2007 and Wang–Zhang 2026 were compared; none states or implies this specific labelled affine coset weight spectrum. Complete all-on minimal-press patterns and weight counts require a separate recurrence/weight analysis. Residual unindexed historical risk and incomplete 2024 induced-matching full-text access are noted.
residual_risks: An indexed or unindexed equivalent formula may exist outside searched literature; no independent priority certification.

value.rationale: The classical all-on Lights Out game asks for a minimum-cardinality solution to (I+A)s=1. For the standard generalized Petersen cubic family, the result identifies a sharp five-divisibility transition, exactly ten optimal strategies when five divides n, and the complete all-on press-count distribution for every n>=5. Even knowledge of the homogeneous quiet-strategy weight enumerator and nullity does not determine this specific affine coset enumerator. The finding provides an exact, natural optimization/strategy benchmark rather than an arbitrary numeric slice.
